missionPremise: P-181 asks what hauska-factory BELIEVES about its input before a bake, and whether any check could see a SHORT fill. The premise it rests on is the Harris incident recorded in the dispatch: dry-run, apply, apply2 and SQL all agreed at 564,948 because all four read the same truncated input, and the membership file's own 536,512 estimate carried the identical bug, so the sizing probe could not contradict the fill. Only an independent derivation, the ZIP central directory, saw it. The companion premise is ENFORCEMENT.md's vacuous-write-path class, whose named instance is computeTier1Envelope in legacy-design-tools: a function that runs, returns a well-formed object, passes its tests, and declines on every branch.
completionPredicate: Done means a stranger can, from the artifact alone and without this agent, (1) name every load-bearing assumption in the parcel-record write paths with a file and line at a declared SHA, (2) say for each whether a guard exists and whether that guard is armed, dormant, starved or vacuous, with its call sites enumerated rather than asserted, (3) say for each rail group whether any check could detect a short fill and whether that check's input is independent of the write path it checks, and (4) know what this review could NOT establish and why. All four are met. A reader who disagrees can falsify any row by opening the cited line at 97b9387.
scopeBasis: Scoped to the parcel-record write paths and the gates that grade them, because that is the machine a bake depends on and the mission named it. INCLUDED beyond the literal file list: publish-readiness-gate.mjs (the only gate that fails closed before a bake, and the dispatch's 17-of-65 context item pointed at it), the CI workflow and the drift guard (the pin question surfaced from ENGINE_PIN.json and could not be answered inside src/), and setback-table-router.mjs (the reachability question for the setback writer cannot be answered without it). EXCLUDED deliberately: the four spine rails' writers, which were not located and are recorded as unexamined rather than absent; the bake and publish jobs themselves, which are downstream of the question; and any live measurement, because the dispatch forbade network and database and because a confident wrong answer here is worse than none. hauska-engine and legacy-design-tools were NOT opened: this lane owns no repo and the seat rule stands.
falsifier: Pre-registered in CP1 before the reads, and three of the pre-registrations came back against my expectation, which is recorded rather than dropped. (1) 'The factory has a vacuous writer' would be falsified by finding a reachable kind:'value' branch in every writer. It WAS falsified: no factory cell writer is vacuous, and the negative is reported first in the artifact. (2) 'publish-gate-sched grades only 17 of 65 rails' would be falsified by DEFAULT_SCHED_RAIL_KEYS deriving from the closed rail set. It WAS falsified at publish-gate-sched.mjs:187. (3) 'setbackFrontFt has no live writer' would be falsified by a reachable value branch. It WAS falsified by parcel-setback-cells.mjs:275-301. The standing falsifier for the report as a whole: open any cited line at 97b9387 and find it says something else, or supply a caller for priorLiveRailKeys, auditNotApplicableCells or assertPublishableCounty, or show that evaluatePopulation refuses on an empty denominator. Any one of those falsifies a headline row.
contradicted: Three carried context items from the dispatch were contradicted at source and are corrected in the artifact rather than repeated. First, the publish gate no longer grades 17 of 65: DEFAULT_SCHED_RAIL_KEYS is the full closed set (publish-gate-sched.mjs:187, P-136 landed); the 17 survive as PUBLISH_FLOOR_RAIL_KEYS in publish-readiness-gate.mjs:145-151, which is the gate that actually fails closed, so the widening did not widen what BLOCKS a bake. Second, write-setback-city.mjs does not exist at this SHA and setbackFrontFt HAS a live writer, contradicting both the dispatch's carried context and publish-gate-sched.mjs:98-107's own in-repo comment, which is stale against its own repo at its own SHA. Third, the verified-context cell-state list is confirmed but the accessPolicy framing is not at issue here. Additionally, two modules in this repo contradict EACH OTHER about the same 46.9 percent figure (publish-readiness-gate.mjs:25-40 versus county-rail-coverage.mjs:13-19) and that disagreement is reported with both readings and adjudicated by neither, because adjudicating another lane's closed finding is not this lane's call.

topFindings: FAC-06 + FAC-01: the pre-bake gate and the rail gate both FAIL OPEN on total absence and fail closed only on partial absence. An empty county produces 65 clean 'excluded' verdicts and a passing pre-bake readiness check, with no error anywhere. Traced link by link, not inferred.

FAC-07 + B.0: the RECORD_FILL_SHORT gate compares parcel_record against landing_parcel_jurisdiction, which is parcel-record-fill's own input AND its own reported denominator. Three of the pipeline's figures read one table. This is the Harris shape, in the gate that exists to prevent it.

FAC-10/11/13: three distinct failure modes (no corpus table, a matcher miss, no parcel geometry) all write `absent-verified`, which is an EARNED kind, so the rail reads live, the gate can pass, and the surface serves 'we looked and there is nothing' about a parcel that has a setback.

FAC-24: a dedicated CI step named 'pin SHA must not move while pin is the control' compares a 64-character sha256 against a 40-character literal and is a tautology in one branch and an assertion about sha256's own output length in the other. Armed and unfalsifiable.

FAC-22 + FAC-23: two disagreeing engine pins (Dockerfile a38cbb2 versus ENGINE_PIN.json dfdf6fd), and the drift guard that would notice reads a WORKING TREE file whenever one exists, ignoring the sha it is named for.

LESSON: A gate written as 'exclude rails nobody has attempted' inverts into 'pass total failure, refuse partial failure' unless liveness is derived from a source OTHER than the cells being graded. hauska-factory has two independent instances of this inversion (evaluateRailGate, evaluatePopulation), which makes it a class rather than a bug.

`absent-verified` is the load-bearing word in this vocabulary and it is the one most easily fabricated, because it is an EARNED kind: writing it turns a rail live, which turns a gate green, which turns on serving. Any writer that emits absent-verified from a branch describing OUR capability rather than the WORLD's state is a serving defect, not a bookkeeping one.

The counting rule for a fill job must distinguish candidate cells from moved cells. Both hauska-factory cell writers compute both numbers and report only the intention, so a run that moves zero rows prints the same success line as one that moves everything.
DEAD-END: Grepping for `kind: "value"` to find vacuous writers is a selector, not evidence: a literal can sit on an unreachable branch. It narrowed 54 files to 9 worth reading and proved nothing on its own.

`git show origin/main:.github/...` fails under MSYS path mangling on this Windows shell (the leading-dot path is rewritten to a Windows path and git reports 'ambiguous argument'). `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*' git show 'origin/main:.github/workflows/ci.yml'` works. Worth knowing before concluding a workflow file is absent.
A bash heredoc large enough to hold a long markdown artifact fails with ENAMETOOLONG on uv_spawn here. Use the Write tool for anything over roughly 15 KB.
